# The Bake Basket

> The Bake Basket (also known as The Bake Basket by Priya) is a fresh-to-order home bakery in Madhavaram, Chennai, Tamil Nadu, India, run by founder and baker Priya Shell. It bakes celebration cakes, bento cakes, cupcakes, brownies, cookies, fresh breads, savoury bakes, millet and no-maida healthy bakes, Chennai fusion flavours such as filter-coffee cake, gift hampers, and traditional South Indian steamed foods such as kozhukattai, vattayappam, ela ada, puttu and idiyappam. Every order is baked after it is placed. Most items can be made eggless. Orders are taken on WhatsApp.

## Key facts
- Name: The Bake Basket (by Priya)
- Tagline: Baked to make your day!
- Founder and baker: Priya Shell
- Address: 229, 1F, AP Achalendra Apartment, Madhavaram Red Hills Highways, Madhavaram, Chennai 600060, Tamil Nadu, India
- Open: Monday to Saturday. Closed on Sundays.
- Orders: WhatsApp +91 90430 27981 (https://wa.me/919043027981); email hello@thebakebasket.com
- Lead time: please order cakes 2 days ahead; festival orders and tiered cakes earlier
- Pickup and delivery: by arrangement; North Chennai neighbourhoods are closest (Madhavaram, Moolakadai, Kolathur, Kodungaiyur, Puzhal, Manali, Perambur, Red Hills)
- Prices: confirmed in writing for each order on WhatsApp
- Payment safety: orders and payments only through +91 90430 27981

# Our Story: Priya Shell, Chennai Home Baker | The Bake Basket
URL: https://thebakebasket.com/our-story/

Home / Our story Our story Love, baked to share Some children follow their mothers to the market. Priya followed the smell of the oven. As a little girl in Chennai she was the one on tiptoe at the kitchen counter, flour on her elbows, asking if she could crack the egg this time. Long before she knew what a talent was, she knew what happened to people's faces when something warm came out of the oven. They softened. They leaned in. They stayed a little longer than they had planned to. Order on WhatsApp See the menu It took her years to understand that this wasn't a hobby she had picked up along the way. It felt more like something she had been trusted with. And the thing about a gift is that it is meant to be given away. It starts before the kitchen Most bakers start with a recipe. Priya starts with a person. When she walks through the market she isn't really shopping. She's picturing faces. The speckled bananas become a loaf for a grandmother who likes something soft with her evening coffee. The dark chocolate becomes brownies a teenager will hide from his brother. The jaggery and grated coconut become kozhukattai for a family that misses how festival mornings used to taste. By the time she's home, the bakes already have names. The names of the people they're for. Knitting flavours together Nothing in her kitchen is rushed and nothing is thrown together. Priya says she knits flavours: a little cardamom worked into a sponge, a pinch of sea salt over caramel, strong filter coffee folded into a frosting, until they hold together like something well made. She measures carefully. She also measures the way mothers do, with her eyes, with her memory, and with one question that every batch has to pass: would I give this to my own children? If the answer is anything less than yes, it doesn't leave her kitchen. Something from nothing There's a small magic in baking that has never worn off for her. Flour, butter, sugar, a few eggs. Ordinary things from an ordinary shelf. Then hands, heat and patience, and suddenly there's a birthday cake that makes a six-year-old gasp, or a loaf that fills a whole flat with the smell of home. She doesn't use ready mixes. She doesn't bake ahead and wait for someone to buy. Your order starts when you place it, so what reaches you is as fresh as what she'd put on her own table. Food says what words can't She has watched it happen again and again. A box of cupcakes that said sorry better than any message could. A tray of soft idiyappam carried to a friend just home from hospital. An anniversary cake that made a couple married forty years laugh like they'd only just met. Food reaches the places words don't. It looks after people. It brings them back to each other. Without a speech, it says: you matter to me. Maybe that's why people who taste her baking rarely ask "how much?" first. They ask, "when can I order again?" Why a basket In every Indian home there's a basket that never stays home. It goes to the temple and the church, to the hospital, to the new baby, to the neighbour on festival morning. A basket is never for yourself. It's how we carry love to someone else. That's The Bake Basket. Priya bakes it. You carry it. And somewhere across the city, someone you love takes the first bite and goes quiet for a moment. That moment is what she bakes for. What I promise you I won't use a ready mix. I won't bake your order before you've placed it. And I won't send you anything I wouldn't serve at my own table. The people behind the blog Priya Shell , founder and baker. Writes about her kitchen, the heritage foods she grew up with, and what actually makes a bake work. Prisha Shell writes about ordering, planning and gifting. Beth Mathew writes about wholesome baking, hosting and festivals. Order from Priya's kitchen with love, Priya Plan your order Please order cakes 2 days ahead. The price is confirmed in writing before I start. WhatsApp Priya More from the menu Celebration cakes Bento cakes Cupcakes Brownies and cookies Fresh breads Healthy bakes Chennai fusion Traditional steamed Eggless menu Savoury bakes Festive hampers Who runs The Bake Basket? The Bake Basket is run by Priya Shell, a mother and home baker in Chennai who bakes every order herself. What makes The Bake Basket different from a regular bakery? Every order is baked only after it's placed, by one person, with ingredients she chooses herself and no ready mixes. The price is confirmed in writing before she starts. Why is it called The Bake Basket? Because in every Indian home a basket is how we carry food to someone else: to the temple, the hospital, the new baby, the neighbour on festival morning. Priya bakes it, you carry it. Does Priya bake traditional South Indian foods as well as cakes? Yes. Alongside cakes and breads she makes steamed foods from Tamil and Kerala kitchens, including kozhukattai, vattayappam, ela ada, puttu and idiyappam.

# Custom Birthday Cakes in Chennai | The Bake Basket
URL: https://thebakebasket.com/cakes/

Home / Menu / Celebration cakes Celebration cakes Celebration cakes, baked for one day: yours A good birthday cake has two jobs. It has to make them gasp when the box opens, and it has to make them go quiet when they take the first bite. Plenty of cakes manage the first. I bake for the second. Every cake starts with a conversation, not a catalogue. Who is it for? How old are they turning? Do they pick the cherries off the Black Forest, or steal everyone else's? Then I bake it for that person, on the day, with real cream and real chocolate, and confirm every detail, and the price, in writing before I start. Plan my cake See the menu For every kind of celebration Children's birthdays. Unicorns, dinosaurs, cricket pitches, their favourite colour in a ridiculous quantity. Theme cakes that still taste like cake, because the six-year-old will eat the frosting and the grandparents will eat the sponge, and both should be happy. First birthdays. Soft, simple sponges with less sugar on request, and smash cakes small enough for tiny hands. Read: Choosing a First Birthday Cake: Smash Cakes, Flavours and Sugar Milestone birthdays and anniversaries. Amma's 60th, your parents' 40th, the colleague who's finally retiring. Elegant floral buttercream, tiered cakes, or one perfect chocolate truffle with their name in a steady hand. Weddings, engagements, baby showers, baptisms and First Communions. Tiered and fondant cakes, planned with you well ahead of the day. The ordinary Tuesday. You don't need a reason. A small cake for no occasion at all is one of the nicest things you can do for a house. Flavours people come back for The classics are classics for a reason. My chocolate truffle is dark, glossy and properly rich, with a sponge that stays moist right to the last slice the next day. The butterscotch has crunch in every forkful. The pineapple tastes of fruit, not of a bottle. Then there are the ones with a little Chennai in them. Filter-coffee mocha, with real decoction folded into the cream, so it smells like a Mylapore kitchen at seven in the morning. Tender coconut, light and milky, for the hot months. Rasmalai and gulab jamun cakes for the family that wants mithai and cake and refuses to choose. Red velvet with a tangy cream cheese frosting. Salted caramel that makes people close their eyes. Biscoff, hazelnut praline, pistachio rose. Ask me which one fits the person and I'll tell you honestly. Which frosting should you choose? Finish Best for Keep in mind Fresh whipped cream Light, classic cakes; most children's flavours Must stay refrigerated; softens quickly in Chennai heat Buttercream Floral designs, piping, richer flavours Holds shape better, richer taste Cream cheese Red velvet, carrot, some fruit cakes Tangy, refrigerate Ganache Chocolate cakes, drip cakes Holds well, intensely chocolatey Fondant Sculpted themes, sharp edges, figurines Mostly for looks; many people peel it off. Not ideal in very humid weather Read: Fondant, Buttercream or Fresh Cream? Choosing a Cake Finish for Chennai Weather How big a cake do you need? A rough guide for party-sized slices: Cake weight Serves Bento (about 300 to 400 g) 2 to 4 500 g 5 to 6 1 kg 10 to 12 1.5 kg 15 to 18 2 kg 20 to 25 3 kg (often tiered) 30 to 35 If dinner is heavy and it's mostly adults, you can stretch it. If there are twelve children and a piñata, don't. Read: How Much Cake Do You Need? A Serving Guide for Every Party Size Eggless cakes Almost every cake here can be made eggless, and I bake my eggless sponges to be just as soft, not as an afterthought. The eggless menu Before you order Notice: please order cakes 2 days ahead. Tiered and detailed fondant work needs more time, so message me as soon as you know the date. During Deepavali, Christmas and the December wedding season, earlier is kinder. Design: send me pictures you love. I'll tell you what will work in the size you need, and what will look better than the picture. Delivery: cream cakes travel cold, flat, and in sturdy boxes. Keep them in the fridge until about 20 minutes before cutting. How to order Start my cake order Plan your order Please order cakes 2 days ahead. The price is confirmed in writing before I start. WhatsApp Priya Helpful reads How Much Cake Do You Need? A Serving Guide for Every Party Size How Far Ahead Should You Order a Custom Cake in Chennai? Fondant, Buttercream or Fresh Cream? Choosing a Cake Finish for Chennai Weather Planning a Kids' Theme Cake That Tastes as Good as It Looks More from the menu Bento cakes Cupcakes Brownies and cookies Fresh breads Healthy bakes Chennai fusion Traditional steamed Eggless menu Savoury bakes Festive hampers How many days in advance should I order a custom cake in Chennai? Please order cakes at least 2 days ahead. Tiered, detailed fondant and wedding cakes need longer, so message as soon as you have a date. During festival weeks and December, book as early as you can. Can you copy a cake design from a picture? Priya can create a cake inspired by your picture, adjusted to the size you need and to what will hold up well. She won't copy another baker's signature design exactly, but she'll make it your own. Do you make cartoon and character theme cakes? Yes, theme cakes are made with your child's favourite colours, hobbies and ideas. Where a design uses a trademarked character, Priya will suggest a theme inspired by it, such as colours and props, rather than a copy. What is the best cake flavour for a kids' birthday party? Chocolate truffle, vanilla with fresh fruit, and butterscotch are the safest crowd-pleasers. For very young children, a lighter vanilla or fruit sponge with less sugar goes down well with parents too. Can I get a cake with less sugar? Yes. Many cakes can be made with reduced sugar, and there are jaggery and date-sweetened cakes on the healthy menu. A reduced-sugar cake still contains sugar, so please don't treat it as diabetic-safe. Will the cake survive the drive across Chennai? Cream cakes are packed cold in sturdy boxes and should travel flat on the car floor with the AC on, not on a seat or a lap. Buttercream and ganache cakes hold up better in the heat than fresh cream.

# Bento Cakes in Chennai, Baked Fresh | The Bake Basket
URL: https://thebakebasket.com/bento-cakes/

Home / Menu / Bento cakes Bento cakes Bento cakes: a small cake for a big feeling Some feelings are too small for a 1 kg cake and too big for a text message. The first anniversary when it's just the two of you. The friend who got the job. The night after the exams. Your sister moving into her first flat, with no plates yet and two forks borrowed from the neighbour. Order a bento cake See the menu That's what a bento cake is for. A little cake, about the size of your palm and a half, in a lunchbox with a spoon tucked in and a few words piped across the top. Enough for two to four people, or one person and a very good evening. Why a small cake works so well There's no leftover cake going stale in the fridge for a week. It's easy to carry on a bike. It fits on the desk at work. And because it's small, you can choose the flavour you actually love instead of the one that pleases twenty people. It's also become the way Chennai says "I thought of you". People send them across the city for no occasion at all, which may be the nicest reason there is. Flavours Chocolate truffle, red velvet, butterscotch, vanilla with berries, Biscoff, salted caramel, filter-coffee mocha, rasmalai and pistachio rose. Most can be made eggless. What to write on top Short wins. The top of a bento is small, so five or six words look best. A few that people love: "Happy 1st, us." "You did it!" "Sorry. Cake?" "Best Amma ever." "Ok fine, you're right." "Welcome home." Read: What to Write on a Birthday Cake: 70 Messages That Fit Plan your order Please order cakes 2 days ahead. The price is confirmed in writing before I start. WhatsApp Priya Helpful reads What Is a Bento Cake, and When Is It the Right Choice? What to Write on a Birthday Cake: 70 Messages That Fit More from the menu Celebration cakes Cupcakes Brownies and cookies Fresh breads Healthy bakes Chennai fusion Traditional steamed Eggless menu Savoury bakes Festive hampers How many people does a bento cake serve? A bento cake is a small cake of roughly 300 to 400 g, enough for two to four people. What is a bento cake? A bento cake is a small cake packed in a lunchbox-style container, usually with a short message piped on top. The idea started in South Korea and is now one of the most popular small gifts in Chennai. Can I get an eggless bento cake? Yes, most bento flavours can be made eggless. Mention it when you order on WhatsApp. Can I send a bento cake to someone as a surprise? Yes. Give us the recipient's address and a delivery window, and we'll deliver it with a handwritten Basket Note. How should I store a bento cake? Keep it in the fridge in its box and take it out about 15 minutes before eating. It's best eaten within a day or two.

# Cupcakes in Chennai, Boxes of 6, 9 and 12 | The Bake Basket
URL: https://thebakebasket.com/cupcakes/

Home / Menu / Everyday treats Everyday treats Cupcakes, one perfect bite at a time A cupcake has no wrong slice. No one gets the corner piece, no one gets the bit without the cherry. Everybody gets their own little cake, frosted all the way to the edge, and there's something about holding a whole one in your hand that makes adults behave like they're seven. That's why cupcakes are what I suggest for school birthdays, office treats, and any party where the children will be running around too fast to sit down for a slice. Order cupcakes See the menu The flavours Classic. Vanilla with a soft swirl of buttercream. Double chocolate that's dark all the way through. Red velvet. Butterscotch with a crunch on top. Filled. Bite into the middle and there's a surprise: Nutella, salted caramel, strawberry jam, or a sharp lemon curd that wakes up the whole cupcake. Indian fusion. Gulab jamun, with a little piece of jamun hiding inside. Rasmalai, soaked and fragrant with saffron. Kesar pista. Filter coffee, for the grown-ups who are only here for the coffee. Sets and gifting Boxes of 6, 9 and 12, mixed or single flavour Mini cupcake boxes for tasting tables and office desks Kids' party sets in your theme colours Floral bouquet cupcakes, piped like a bunch of flowers, for Mother's Day and anniversaries Festive boxes for Deepavali, Christmas and Eid For school birthdays Many schools now ask for individually portioned treats. Cupcakes are perfect: no knife, no plates, no mess for the teacher. Tell me the number of children and any nut rules at the school, and I'll keep them simple, small and easy to share. Plan your order Please order cakes 2 days ahead. The price is confirmed in writing before I start. WhatsApp Priya Helpful reads Edible Return Gifts for Kids' Birthday Parties The Kids' Birthday Party Food Checklist More from the menu Celebration cakes Bento cakes Brownies and cookies Fresh breads Healthy bakes Chennai fusion Traditional steamed Eggless menu Savoury bakes Festive hampers How many cupcakes should I order for a class birthday? Order one per child plus three or four extra for teachers and the inevitable second helping. For a class of 30, a box of 36 works well. Can I order mixed flavours in one box? Yes. Boxes of 9 and 12 can be mixed, for example three each of four flavours. Do you make eggless cupcakes? Yes, most cupcake flavours can be made eggless. What is a cupcake bouquet? A cupcake bouquet is a set of cupcakes piped to look like flowers and arranged together like a bunch, often used as a Mother's Day, anniversary or thank-you gift. How long do cupcakes stay fresh? Buttercream cupcakes are best within a day or two. Keep them in a cool room, or in the fridge in a sealed box if your house is warm, and bring them to room temperature before serving.

# Eggless Cakes and Bakes in Chennai | The Bake Basket
URL: https://thebakebasket.com/eggless/

Home / Menu / Eggless menu Eggless menu Eggless, and you'd never know In a lot of Chennai homes, the cake question comes with a second question attached. "Is it eggless?" Sometimes it's Paati. Sometimes it's a fasting day, or a Jain friend, or a child with an egg allergy, or simply a family that has never eaten eggs and never will. I don't think anyone at a celebration should be handed the "other" cake. So I bake my eggless sponges to stand on their own: soft, springy, moist enough to stay good the next morning. Most guests can't tell which one is eggless. Some of them prefer it. Order eggless See the menu What can be eggless Cakes: nearly every flavour, from chocolate truffle and butterscotch to red velvet and rasmalai Bento cakes: most flavours Cupcakes: classic, filled and fusion Brownies: fudgy, walnut and most of the range Cookies: butter cookies, nankhatai, choco-chip and more Breads: ask which loaves are egg-free; many breads contain no egg to begin with Heritage foods: kozhukattai, puttu, idiyappam and ela ada are made without egg What goes in instead Eggs do a few jobs in a cake. They hold it together, help it rise and keep it moist. In my eggless bakes, those jobs go to things your grandmother would recognise: curd, milk, a little oil or butter, and the right balance of raising agents. Read: What Replaces Eggs in an Eggless Cake, and Why It's Still Soft An honest note about my kitchen My kitchen bakes with eggs too. I use separate bowls and utensils and wash everything well between batches, but I can't promise the trace-free conditions of a kitchen that never sees an egg. If someone has a severe egg allergy, or your family follows strict rules about this, please tell me, and we'll talk it through properly before you order. A well-made eggless cake is just as soft and moist. The Bake Basket's eggless sponges use curd and milk to give a fine, tender crumb, and most guests can't tell the difference. Can I get an eggless cake for a Jain family? The cake itself can be made eggless. No. Eggless bakes usually still contain milk, butter or curd. Vegan cakes contain no animal products at all. If you need vegan, ask before you order. Is it safe to order eggless if my child has an egg allergy? Eggless bakes are made in a kitchen that also uses eggs, so there is a small risk of cross-contact. Lunchbox Bakes Chennai Kids Will Actually Eat More from the menu Celebration cakes Bento cakes Cupcakes Brownies and cookies Healthy bakes Chennai fusion Traditional steamed Eggless menu Savoury bakes Festive hampers How long does homemade bread last? Without preservatives, homemade bread is best within two to three days. Keep it in a bread bag or cloth at room temperature, or slice and freeze it and toast straight from the freezer. Is sourdough healthier than regular bread? Sourdough's long fermentation can make it easier for some people to digest and gives it a lower glycaemic impact than many white breads, but it is still bread. It's a better everyday choice, not a health food. Should I keep bread in the fridge in Chennai? The fridge dries bread out faster. In Chennai's humidity, keep it in a cool, dry spot for a day or two, and freeze anything you won't eat by then. Can I order bread every week? Home / Menu / Healthy bakes Healthy bakes Dessert for the whole table At most family birthdays there's one person who says "just a small piece for me", and then doesn't have one. Jaggery cakes, date-sweetened cakes, honey oat cookies. Whole grain. Whole-wheat cakes, oats cookies, multigrain loaves. Diet-specific. Eggless range, reduced-sugar cakes, high-protein bars. Gluten-free and vegan bakes: please ask before ordering. For lunchboxes. Lunchbox muffins, veggie muffins, nut-free school cookies. What these bakes are, and what they aren't I'd rather tell you plainly than sell you a word. Jaggery, dates and honey are still sugar. They bring flavour and a little more mineral content than white sugar, but your blood sugar still responds to them. A jaggery cake is a better treat. It is not a sugar-free one. "Reduced sugar" means less sugar than my regular recipe , and I'll tell you how much less. It doesn't mean none. Ragi is naturally gluten-free, but many ragi bakes include wheat flour for texture. If you need gluten-free, tell me, and I'll tell you exactly which bakes are and how they're made. Millets add fibre and a deeper, nuttier taste. They make a treat more filling, which usually means people eat less of it without trying. If someone at home has diabetes, these are the bakes to choose, in a small portion, with their doctor's advice in mind. I'm a baker, not a doctor, and I won't pretend otherwise. # Kozhukattai & Vattayappam in Chennai | The Bake Basket
URL: https://thebakebasket.com/traditional-steamed-foods/

Home / Menu / Traditional steamed Traditional steamed The steamed foods of a South Indian home, made the slow way Some foods aren't really recipes. They're mornings. Kozhukattai on Vinayagar Chathurthi, the first one set aside for the offering before anyone in the house is allowed to eat. Vattayappam on Christmas morning, soft and sweet and smelling of cardamom, cut into wedges beside the beef fry or the stew. Ela ada at Onam, unwrapped from a banana leaf with the steam curling up, coconut and jaggery spilling out the moment you bite. Order heritage foods See the menu Most of us grew up with these. Fewer of us have the time, or the steamer, or Amma standing beside us telling us when the dough is right. So I make them the way they were made in our grandmothers' kitchens: rice soaked and ground, coconut grated fresh, jaggery melted slowly, everything steamed, nothing rushed. From Tamil kitchens Kozhukattai. Soft rice-flour shells around a filling of coconut and jaggery, cardamom-scented, steamed until the outside turns faintly translucent. Sweet, or savoury with a spiced urad dal filling. Pidi kozhukattai. Pressed in the fist, so each one carries the shape of the hand that made it. Idli. Rava, millet, and Kanchipuram idli, spiced with pepper, cumin and ginger, with the richness of ghee. Idiyappam. Fine, soft string hoppers, for stew, coconut milk or sweetened coconut. Paniyaram. Crisp outside, soft inside, sweet or savoury. From Kerala kitchens Vattayappam. A soft, spongy steamed rice cake, fermented overnight, sweetened and scented with cardamom, often studded with raisins and cashews. Made for Christmas and Easter, and for any Sunday that deserves it. Ela ada. Rice parcels filled with coconut and jaggery, folded into banana leaf and steamed. The leaf leaves its smell on everything, which is the point. Puttu. Steamed cylinders of rice, ragi or wheat flour layered with fresh coconut. With kadala curry, or banana and sugar. Kinnathappam. A gentle, sliceable steamed sweet from Malabar, smooth and fragrant with coconut milk. For festivals Vinayagar Chathurthi: sweet and savoury kozhukattai, modak Onam: ela ada and festive sweets Christmas and Easter: vattayappam The steamer only holds so much, and festival mornings come for everyone at once. Please book festival orders as early as you can, ideally a week ahead. Plan your order Please order cakes 2 days ahead. The price is confirmed in writing before I start. Kerala's Soft Steamed Cake for Christmas and Easter Ela Ada: The Banana-Leaf Sweet That Tastes Like Onam Puttu, Idiyappam and Appam: A Guide to Kerala's Steamed Breakfasts More from the menu Celebration cakes Bento cakes Cupcakes Brownies and cookies Fresh breads Healthy bakes Chennai fusion Eggless menu Savoury bakes Festive hampers Where can I order kozhukattai in Chennai for Vinayagar Chathurthi? The Bake Basket takes advance orders for sweet and savoury kozhukattai and modak for Vinayagar Chathurthi. Order on WhatsApp about a week before the festival so your batch can be steamed fresh for the day. What is vattayappam? Vattayappam is a soft, steamed rice cake from Kerala, made from fermented rice batter with coconut and sugar and flavoured with cardamom. It is traditionally made for Christmas and Easter, especially in Syrian Christian homes. What is the difference between kozhukattai and modak? Both are steamed rice-flour dumplings with a coconut and jaggery filling. Kozhukattai is the Tamil name and style, often shaped by hand; modak is the Maharashtrian name, usually pleated into a pointed top. How long do steamed foods stay fresh? Steamed rice foods are best on the day they're made. Kozhukattai and ada keep in the fridge for a day; steam them again for a couple of minutes to bring back their softness. Can I order heritage foods outside of festivals? Yes. Puttu, idiyappam, idli, kozhukattai and vattayappam can be ordered year-round for family meals, guests and Sunday breakfasts. Are your steamed foods eggless? Kozhukattai, ela ada, puttu, idiyappam and idli are made without egg. Ask about vattayappam and kinnathappam when you order.

# Kerala Plum Cake in Chennai | The Bake Basket
URL: https://thebakebasket.com/christmas-plum-cake/

Home / Menu / Christmas Christmas The Christmas plum cake, soaked and baked the old way The fruit goes into its jar weeks before Christmas. Raisins, dates, orange peel, cherries, a handful of cashews, all left to soak and darken while the rest of the year carries on. By the time it reaches the batter, the fruit has turned soft and almost jammy, and the whole kitchen smells of cinnamon, clove and nutmeg. Then comes the caramel. Sugar cooked dark and slow until it's nearly bitter, which is what gives a Kerala plum cake its deep brown colour and that faint burnt-sugar note you can taste under the spice. Book my plum cake See the menu It's a cake that gets better with time. Slice it on Christmas Eve, and it's lovely. Slice it on the 27th, after it's sat wrapped for a few days, and it's even better. Sizes and options: ask on WhatsApp. Order by: mid November for Christmas week. Pair it with vattayappam and butter cookies for a full Christmas basket. Kerala's Soft Steamed Cake for Christmas and Easter More from the menu Celebration cakes Bento cakes Cupcakes Brownies and cookies Fresh breads Healthy bakes Chennai fusion Traditional steamed Eggless menu Savoury bakes Festive hampers How long does a plum cake last? A well-wrapped rich plum cake keeps for two to three weeks at cool room temperature, and longer in the fridge. Alcohol-soaked cakes keep longer than alcohol-free ones. Is there an alcohol-free plum cake? Ask when you book. An alcohol-free plum cake uses fruit soaked in juice, and has the same spice and colour. What's the difference between plum cake and fruit cake? In India, "plum cake" usually means a rich, spiced, dark fruit cake made at Christmas. It contains dried fruit like raisins and dates rather than fresh plums; the name comes from the old English use of "plum" for raisins. When should I order my Christmas plum cake? Baked fresh on the day Your order is baked for you, not before you order and not for anyone else. Then it's ready for pickup from our kitchen in Madhavaram, or delivered by arrangement. How far ahead to order Please order cakes 2 days ahead. That gives the sponge time to bake and cool properly, and the decoration time to be done with care. For tiered and detailed fondant cakes, gift hampers in quantity and festival orders such as kozhukattai, plum cake or Deepavali baskets, message me as early as you can, ideally a week ahead. The oven and the steamer only hold so much, and festival mornings arrive for everyone at once. Last minute? Message anyway. If I can do it properly, I will. If I can't, I'll tell you, rather than rush something that matters to you. North Chennai neighbourhoods are closest; for other parts of the city, tell me your area and we'll work out what's possible. Delivery areas We're open Monday to Saturday. We're closed on Sundays. When your order arrives Put cream and buttercream cakes straight into the fridge, and take them out about 20 minutes before cutting. Brownies and cookies are happy in an airtight box. Steamed foods are best the same day. If you're carrying a cake in a car, keep it flat on the floor with the AC on, never on a seat or a lap. Questions about a particular bake live on that bake's own page; ordering questions are on How to Order. Order on WhatsApp See the menu Where is The Bake Basket? The Bake Basket is a home bakery at 229, 1F, AP Achalendra Apartment, Madhavaram Red Hills Highways, Madhavaram, Chennai 600060. It's run by founder and baker Priya Shell. Do you use ready mixes? No. Cakes are made from scratch, with real butter, good chocolate and honest flour, and baked fresh after you order. What allergens should I mention when I order? Tell us about any allergy to eggs, nuts, peanuts, gluten, dairy or soy. The kitchen handles all of these, so Priya will explain honestly what she can and can't guarantee. Is the eggless range made in a separate kitchen? No. Eggless bakes are made in the same home kitchen that uses eggs, with separate bowls and careful washing. For severe allergies or strict observance, talk to Priya before ordering. Can I add a personal message? Yes. Cakes can carry a short piped message, and longer words fit on the handwritten note that comes with your order. What if it rains on my delivery day? Chennai rain happens. Orders are packed to travel safely, and if heavy rain affects a delivery we'll message you before the agreed time, not after. Do you bake for events and pop-ups? Yes, when the date allows. Email hello@thebakebasket.com with the event, date and number of guests. Who writes the blog? Priya Shell, Prisha Shell and Beth Mathew write the blog: baking know-how, planning guides, festival foods and gifting ideas.

# Privacy Policy | The Bake Basket
URL: https://thebakebasket.com/privacy-policy/

Home / Legal Legal Privacy policy This policy explains what personal details The Bake Basket uses, why, and what you can ask us to do with them. Last updated: 26 November 2026. Order on WhatsApp See the menu What we collect When you order, we use the details you send us: your name, phone number, delivery address, the order itself, any diet or allergy notes, and the messages we exchange on WhatsApp, by phone or by email. When you visit this website, Google Analytics, loaded through Google Tag Manager, records anonymous usage such as pages viewed and the type of device, using cookies. Why we use it To plan, bake and deliver your order, to reply to you, and to understand which pages help people find what they need. We don't sell your details, and we don't send marketing messages unless you ask us to. Who we share it with Only the people who help us complete your order, such as a delivery person who needs your address and phone number, and the services we use to run the website (GitHub for hosting, Google for analytics). WhatsApp, payment apps and email providers handle messages under their own privacy terms. How long we keep it Order messages are kept for as long as they're useful for your future orders and our records, and then deleted. Analytics data is kept according to the Google Analytics retention settings. Your choices You can ask us what details we hold about you, ask us to correct them, or ask us to delete them, by emailing hello@thebakebasket.com or messaging +91 90430 27981. You can block or delete cookies in your browser at any time. Contact The Bake Basket, 229, 1F, AP Achalendra Apartment, Madhavaram Red Hills Highways, Madhavaram, Chennai 600060. Email hello@thebakebasket.com.

# Allergen Information | The Bake Basket
URL: https://thebakebasket.com/allergen-information/

Home / Allergens Allergens Allergen information The Bake Basket is a home kitchen, and it handles common allergens every day. Please read this before ordering for someone with an allergy. Last updated: 26 November 2026. Order on WhatsApp See the menu Allergens in our kitchen Eggs, milk and dairy, wheat and gluten, tree nuts, peanuts, soy and sesame are all used in our kitchen. What eggless, nut-free and gluten-free mean here Eggless bakes contain no egg, but they're made in a kitchen that also uses eggs. Nut-free bakes contain no nuts as ingredients, but nuts are used in the same kitchen. Ragi and millet bakes may contain wheat unless we agree a wheat-free version with you. We use separate utensils and clean carefully, but we can't promise a kitchen free of traces. Tell us before you order If someone has an allergy, tell us when you order, with as much detail as you can. For severe allergies, we'll talk it through properly, and if we can't make something safely, we'll say so.

WhatsApp Priya Helpful reads How to keep a cake fresh in Chennai heat How far ahead to order a custom cake How much cake do you need? Do you deliver to Thiruvottiyur? Yes. Thiruvottiyur is about 11 km from our kitchen, and delivery is arranged with each order. Can steamed foods be delivered to Thiruvottiyur? Yes. We time the steaming close to delivery. Re-steam for a couple of minutes at home to bring back the softness. How far ahead should I order festival foods? About a week ahead for festival mornings, and at least 2 days ahead for cakes.

# How Much Cake Do You Need? A Serving Guide for Every Party Size
URL: https://thebakebasket.com/blog/how-much-cake-do-i-need/

For most parties, plan on about 100 grams of cake per guest. That means a 1 kg cake for 10 to 12 people, 2 kg for 20 to 25, and 3 kg for around 30 to 35. The rest of this post explains when to round up, when you can safely round down, and why the answer for a children's party is not the same as the answer for a wedding reception. If you already know your numbers and just want to talk flavours, our custom cakes page has everything else. The quick table Guests Cake weight Notes --------- 2 to 4 Bento cake (300 to 400 g) Perfect for couples, small families, "just us" evenings 5 to 6 500 g A small family birthday 10 to 12 1 kg The most common size we bake 15 to 18 1.5 kg Medium gatherings 20 to 25 2 kg Usually still a single tier 30 to 35 3 kg Often better as two tiers 40 to 50 4 to 5 kg Tiered, or one cake plus cupcakes 75 to 100 7 to 10 kg Tiered display cake, sometimes with a kitchen cake for cutting These are party slices, roughly 80 to 100 g each. Wedding-style "finger slices" are smaller, closer to 50 g, which is why a wedding cake can stretch further than a birthday cake of the same weight. When to round up Children's parties. You'd think little people eat little slices. They don't, partly because the slice is mostly frosting and they want another one, and partly because parents end up eating a slice "to help finish it". For a party of 15 children and 10 adults, I'd plan for 25 full servings and add half a kilo. When cake is the main event. An afternoon birthday at home, with snacks and tea rather than a meal, means people come back for seconds. Add 20%. Teenagers. Enough said. If you want leftovers. Some families want a slice for the next morning and a box to send to the neighbour. Decide that up front, because it's cheaper to bake a bigger cake than a second one. When you can round down After a heavy dinner. If the cake comes out after biryani and two kinds of dessert, many guests will take a sliver or skip it. You can plan on 70% of your headcount. Rich cakes. A dense chocolate truffle, a cheesecake or a rich plum cake is cut thinner than a light vanilla sponge. People simply don't want a big piece. A 1 kg cheesecake can serve 14 easily. Mostly older guests. Many will want a small piece, especially if there are diabetic family members. This is where a smaller cake plus a tray of reduced-sugar or millet bakes works beautifully. Cupcakes change the maths Cupcakes are one serving each, which makes planning easy and portion control automatic. For school birthdays, cupcakes are often better than a big cake because the teacher doesn't have to cut and plate anything. Count one per child plus a few extra for staff. A popular combination for larger parties: a smaller "cutting cake" for the photos and candles, then cupcakes for serving. A 1.5 kg cake plus 36 cupcakes looks generous for 50 guests, costs less than a 5 kg tiered cake, and nobody waits in a queue for a slice. Office parties At work, people take a slice, chat, and go back to their desks. Plan on 80 g per person and choose a flavour almost everyone likes. Chocolate truffle and butterscotch are the safest. Ask about eggless needs before you order; in most Chennai offices, the eggless question decides the order, so many teams simply go fully eggless. Our corporate orders page has more on this. A note on tiers People often assume a tiered cake means a bigger cake. Not always. Tiers are about height and drama as much as quantity. A 3 kg cake can be a wide single tier or a taller two-tier. If you're expecting 30 guests and want a cake that photographs well, two tiers will look grander. If the cake is mostly for eating, one wide tier is easier to cut and serve. The real question When I talk to people planning a party, the number of guests is usually the easy part. The trickier question is how much of a moment the cake should be. Is it something everyone gathers around while the lights go off and the song starts? Or is it dessert after dinner? If it's the moment, go a little bigger and make it beautiful. If it's dessert, buy for appetite, not for show. And if you're unsure, message us with your guest list and the menu. We'll suggest a size, and we'll tell you if you're about to over-order. How many people does a 1 kg cake serve? A 1 kg cake serves about 10 to 12 people with standard party slices, or up to 15 to 18 with thin wedding-style slices. How much cake do I need for 50 guests? For 50 guests, plan on 4 to 5 kg of cake, usually as a two- or three-tier cake. A smaller cutting cake plus cupcakes is a popular, cheaper alternative. Should I order extra cake for a kids' birthday party? Yes. Children often take second helpings and parents eat too, so count every child and adult as a full serving and add about half a kilo.

---

# How Far Ahead Should You Order a Custom Cake in Chennai?
URL: https://thebakebasket.com/blog/how-far-ahead-to-order-custom-cake/

For most cakes from a home baker in Chennai, two days' notice is enough; that's what we ask at The Bake Basket. For detailed fondant or tiered cakes, give a week or more. For a wedding cake, start talking four to eight weeks out. And for anything in Deepavali week, Christmas week or the December wedding season, book as soon as you know the date. That's the short version. Here's why, and what to do if you're reading this on a Thursday for a Saturday party. Why a home baker needs more notice than a shop A bakery with a counter is baking all the time. There are sponges in the walk-in fridge, frosting in tubs, and a team of people. When you walk in, they finish a cake that was mostly made already. A fresh-to-order home baker works differently. At The Bake Basket, nothing gets baked until you order it. That's the whole point: your cake isn't sitting around waiting for you. But it also means each order takes up real time on a real calendar, and there's one oven and one pair of hands. Here's what actually happens to a custom cake over a few days: - Day 1: you share the idea and photos. We talk size, flavour, design, eggless or not. - Day 2: the design is confirmed. Any special ingredients, toppers or colours are bought. Fondant figures, if any, are made now so they can dry and hold their shape. - Day before: the sponge is baked and cooled completely. A warm sponge melts frosting. - The day: filling, frosting, decoration, chilling, the photo for you, and out the door. Rush that and something gives. Usually it's the decoration, sometimes it's the texture, and occasionally it's the baker's sleep, which you don't want either. Lead times, by type of cake What you're ordering Comfortable notice ------ Brownies, cookies, breads 1 to 2 days Bento cake, standard flavour 1 to 2 days Celebration cake, simple design 2 days Custom theme cake (cream or buttercream) 2 to 4 days Fondant theme cake with figures 5 to 7 days Tiered cake 1 to 2 weeks Wedding or engagement cake 4 to 8 weeks (to plan, taste and book) Festival orders (kozhukattai, plum cake, hampers) 1 to 3 weeks before the festival The busy seasons Some weeks fill up quickly in Chennai and it's worth knowing them in advance. Deepavali. Hampers and cookie boxes for families, neighbours and offices. Corporate orders start arriving three or four weeks before. December. Christmas plum cakes, Christmas parties, New Year, and the peak of the wedding and reception season, all at once. If you have a December date, book in November. Vinayagar Chathurthi. Kozhukattai and modak orders for the same morning. A steamer holds only so many at a time. See our traditional steamed foods page. Mother's Day, Valentine's Day. Smaller orders, but lots of them on one date. The school calendar. End of term and the start of the academic year bring class parties and teachers' gifts. If it's last minute It happens. The party moved forward, the office forgot, or someone casually mentioned that today is their birthday. Message anyway. Some things can be done quickly and done well: brownies, a simple cream cake, a bento with a message, a cookie box. What usually can't be rushed is anything with fondant, sculpted shapes, tiers or very specific colours. A good baker will tell you honestly what's possible. If someone agrees to a three-tier fondant cake for tomorrow, be a little suspicious about where that cake came from. How to make ordering faster When you message, send these four things in your first message and you'll save a day of back and forth: 1. Date, time and delivery area 2. Number of guests 3. Flavour, or "help me choose" 4. Two or three pictures of designs you like, and anything you definitely don't want Mention eggless, allergies, or a budget up front too. It changes the suggestions. How many days before should I order a birthday cake? At The Bake Basket, please order cakes 2 days ahead, and a week ahead for detailed fondant designs. Can I order a custom cake one day before? Sometimes. Simple cream cakes, bento cakes and brownies can often be made at one day's notice, but detailed fondant or tiered designs need more time to be done properly. When should I book a wedding cake in Chennai? Start four to eight weeks ahead to allow time for design discussion and a tasting. For December weddings, book earlier, as it's the busiest season.

# Fondant, Buttercream or Fresh Cream? Choosing a Cake Finish for Chennai Weather
URL: https://thebakebasket.com/blog/fondant-vs-buttercream-vs-fresh-cream/

If you want a cake that tastes light and creamy, choose fresh whipped cream. If you want piped flowers and a cake that holds its shape better in heat, choose buttercream or ganache. Choose fondant only when the design truly needs smooth sculpted surfaces or figures, and know that many people peel it off before eating. That's what I tell people on WhatsApp almost every day. Here's the longer version, from someone who has watched all four of them meet a Chennai afternoon. Fresh whipped cream This is the cake most of us grew up with. The pineapple cake at a cousin's birthday, the Black Forest with cherries, the slice that came home wrapped in a paper napkin. Whipped cream is light, barely sweet, and cool on the tongue. It's what makes a sponge cake feel like a celebration instead of a heavy dessert. Children love it, and so do grandparents, who often find buttercream too rich. Its weakness is heat. Whipped cream is mostly air and fat, and Chennai is mostly heat and humidity. Leave a fresh cream cake out on the dining table at 3 pm in May and within half an hour the edges begin to slump. Nothing is wrong with the cake. It's just physics. Choose fresh cream when the cake goes straight from the box into the fridge and comes out shortly before cutting, and when the design is soft: rosettes, fruit, simple writing, a gentle drip. Buttercream Buttercream is butter beaten with sugar until it's pale and smooth, sometimes with a little cream or milk. It's richer than whipped cream and more stable. You can pipe crisp petals with it, build ruffles, and get those smooth, sharp-edged cakes you see in pictures. It handles heat better than whipped cream, though it softens too if left in the sun. In an air-conditioned hall, a buttercream cake will sit happily through speeches and photos. The taste is fuller and sweeter. I balance it with flavour so it never tastes like sweet grease: salted caramel, coffee, dark chocolate, a little citrus. Done well, buttercream tastes of butter, which is to say, of something good. Choose buttercream for floral cakes, elegant anniversary and milestone cakes, and any cake that will sit out for a while before it's cut. Ganache Ganache is chocolate melted into hot cream, then cooled until it thickens. It sets firm and glossy and gives the sharpest edges of all the soft finishes. It's what makes a drip cake drip. For chocolate lovers it's the best finish there is. It's also the most heat-tolerant of the creamy options, especially with dark chocolate. If you're worried about the cake surviving the drive across the city, a dark ganache cake is the brave choice. Fondant Fondant is a sugar paste rolled out thin and draped over a cake, usually on top of a layer of buttercream or ganache. It gives a perfectly smooth surface that can be coloured, shaped and sculpted. Cricket bats, cartoon houses, sharp geometric tiers, figures standing on top: that's fondant. The truth about fondant is that it's mostly there for the eyes. It tastes sweet and a little chewy, and in my experience at least half the guests set it aside on their plate. The cake inside is what they eat. In Chennai's humidity, fondant can also become sticky and "sweat" if a chilled cake is brought into a warm room. The trick is to keep fondant cakes in a cool, air-conditioned room rather than going in and out of the fridge, unless the filling needs refrigeration, in which case we plan the cake differently. Choose fondant when the design is the gift: a child's full theme, a sculpted cake, or a figure that matters. A side-by-side Fresh cream Buttercream Ganache Fondant --------------- Taste Light, airy, mildly sweet Rich, buttery, sweeter Deep chocolate Sweet, chewy Holds in heat Poorly Moderately Well Well, but sweats with temperature change Best for Classic flavours, kids, grandparents Florals, milestone cakes, piping Chocolate lovers, drip cakes, long drives Sculpted themes, figures, sharp tiers Fridge? Always Usually Yes, then rest before serving Keep cool, avoid in-and-out of fridge What I actually recommend For most birthdays at home, fresh cream or a light buttercream, depending on the flavour. For a cake that has to sit in a hall, buttercream or ganache. For a child who has dreamed about a specific theme for months, a cake that uses fondant only where it's needed, for the figures or the topper, with a buttercream or cream finish everywhere else. That way the picture still works and the cake still gets eaten. Not sure? Tell me where the cake will be, how long it'll sit before cutting, and who's eating it. I'll suggest the finish. You can browse ideas on our cakes page. Which cake frosting is best for hot weather? Dark chocolate ganache and buttercream hold up best in heat. Fresh whipped cream softens quickly, so it needs to stay refrigerated until shortly before serving. Does fondant taste good? Fondant is very sweet and slightly chewy. Many people enjoy it in small amounts, but it's mainly used for appearance, and plenty of guests peel it off. Is buttercream heavier than whipped cream? Yes. Buttercream is made from butter and sugar, so it's richer and sweeter. Whipped cream is lighter and less sweet.

---

# What Is a Bento Cake, and When Is It the Right Choice?
URL: https://thebakebasket.com/blog/what-is-a-bento-cake/

A bento cake is a small cake, usually around 300 to 400 grams and about 10 cm across, packed in a lunchbox-style container with a short message piped on top. It serves two to four people. The idea comes from South Korea, where "lunchbox cakes" became a popular small gift, and it has spread across India over the last few years, Chennai included. If you already know you want one, our bento cakes page has the flavours. If you're deciding whether it's the right choice, read on. Why the name "Bento" is the Japanese word for a packed lunch in a box, and it's become a general word for a meal packed neatly in a container. The cake gets the name because it travels in a little clamshell box, like a lunch. Many come with a small fork or spoon, which tells you how they're meant to be eaten: straight from the box, together, with no plates. Why they caught on A few things came together. They're the right size for how many of us live now. A couple in a flat, a small family, a group of three friends. A 1 kg cake for two people means five days of leftover cake slowly drying in the fridge. They're easy to send. A bento fits on the seat of a two-wheeler, on an office desk, on the table of a hostel room. They're good for messages. The top is small and flat, which makes it perfect for a few words. "You did it." "Sorry." "Happy 1st, us." And they look lovely in photos, which never hurts. When a bento cake is the right choice For two to four people. Anniversaries, a small family birthday, a "just us" night. For "I thought of you". A congratulations, a get-well, a thank-you, a sorry. The size makes it feel personal instead of extravagant. For a second cake. A big party cake for the guests and a little bento just for the birthday person, with their name, to cut alone with their family before everyone arrives. For the office. A bento on a colleague's desk on their birthday morning is a small thing people remember for years. For trying a new flavour. Want to see if your family likes filter-coffee mocha before ordering it for the big party? Try a bento. When it isn't If you have more than five or six people, a bento is going to feel stingy, and someone will end up with a teaspoon of cake. For eight people, order a 750 g to 1 kg cake instead, or two bentos in different flavours, which is a nice way to give people a choice. It's also not the right format for a big, detailed design. The surface is small. A few words, a simple drawing, some piped flowers, yes. A full theme with figures, no. Flavours that suit a small cake Because a bento is small, rich flavours work brilliantly. Chocolate truffle, salted caramel, Biscoff, red velvet with cream cheese. Fruit flavours work well too, especially in summer. Many of our bento flavours can also be made eggless. What to write on one Keep it to four to six words. Long messages get squashed into tiny letters. Some favourites: - "Happy birthday, Appa" - "Still you. Always." - "Proud of you" - "Welcome to the world" - "Okay, you win" There are seventy more ideas in our post on what to write on a cake. How to keep it A bento cake is usually a cream or buttercream cake, so keep it in the fridge in its box and take it out 10 to 15 minutes before eating. Eat it within a day or two. How many people does a bento cake serve? A bento cake serves two to four people. It typically weighs about 300 to 400 grams. Where did bento cakes come from? Bento cakes, also called lunchbox cakes, became popular in South Korea as small, personal gift cakes packed in takeaway-style boxes, and the trend spread to India through social media. Is a bento cake cheaper than a regular cake? A bento cake costs less in total because it's much smaller, though the price per kilo is usually higher because of the decoration and packaging.

---

# Choosing a First Birthday Cake: Smash Cakes, Flavours and Sugar
URL: https://thebakebasket.com/blog/first-birthday-cake-guide/

A good first birthday cake does two jobs. There's the big cake for family and guests, and, if you like, a small "smash cake" just for the baby, made softer and simpler, with less sugar and no hard decorations. Most families in Chennai now do one or both. Either way, the baby will mostly remember none of it, and you will remember all of it, so it's worth getting right. Is a first birthday cake safe for a baby? At one year, most babies have started on family foods, and a small taste of cake on their birthday is a joyful tradition rather than a nutritional event. Paediatric advice generally recommends keeping added sugar very low for children under two, so it makes sense to keep the baby's portion small and the recipe gentle. Talk to your paediatrician if your baby has any allergies or a restricted diet. A few practical rules for the baby's cake: - No whole nuts, hard sugar decorations, toothpicks, wires or inedible toppers anywhere the baby can reach. - Avoid honey in anything a baby under one year eats. If the birthday falls right on the first birthday, it's simplest to skip honey in the baby's portion entirely. - Watch for common allergens you haven't introduced yet: egg, nuts, peanuts. If the baby hasn't had egg, ask for an eggless cake for the smash cake. - Go easy on food colouring. Pale, natural colours look lovely in photos anyway. What's a smash cake? A smash cake is a small cake, usually about 10 to 12 cm across, made for the baby to dig into with both hands. The idea is simple: put the baby, the cake and a camera together, and see what happens. Some babies dive straight in. Some poke it once, look offended, and burst into tears. Both make good photos. For a smash cake, I suggest: - A soft vanilla, banana or carrot sponge - A light whipped cream or yogurt-based frosting, rather than thick buttercream - Reduced sugar, or naturally sweetened with banana or dates (still sugar, but gentler) - One soft colour, no fondant Flavours for the main cake The main cake is for the guests, and in a typical Chennai first birthday, that means grandparents, aunts, uncles, cousins and a lot of other children. Choose something that pleases a wide range: - Vanilla with fresh fruit: light, pretty, safe for everyone - Chocolate truffle: the crowd favourite with older children and adults - Butterscotch: reliably loved across generations - Pineapple: a nostalgic classic - Rasmalai or pista: for families who want something Indian If several older family members are watching their sugar, consider a smaller main cake plus a tray of millet or jaggery bakes. Our healthy bakes are made for exactly that kind of table. Theme and design First birthdays often have a theme: a colour, an animal, "ONEderland", a favourite nursery rhyme, the moon and stars. A cake that matches the backdrop makes the photos feel complete. Some ideas that look beautiful and stay simple: - A large "1" number cake in soft pastels - A cake topped with a fondant version of the baby's favourite soft toy (on the guests' cake, not the baby's) - A half-and-half cake for babies born around the six-month mark of a festival or season - A floral buttercream cake with the baby's name - Clouds, stars and moons for a "little star" theme Send your baker the invitation or a photo of the decorations. It helps more than any description. How big? Count everyone, including children, and add a little for the baby's grandparents, who will want to take some home. A typical first birthday at home with 25 to 30 guests needs about 2.5 to 3 kg of cake. In a hall with 60 to 80 guests, think 5 to 7 kg, or a smaller cake plus cupcakes. There's a full guide in how much cake do you need. Timing on the day Babies don't care about your schedule. Plan the cake cutting for when the baby is usually awake and fed, not after the afternoon nap they skipped. Keep the smash cake in the fridge until five minutes before, have a towel and a change of clothes ready, and accept that the outfit you bought specially will not survive. What is the best cake flavour for a first birthday? For the baby's own cake, a soft vanilla, banana or carrot sponge with light cream and reduced sugar works well. For guests, vanilla with fruit, chocolate truffle and butterscotch are the most popular choices. Can a one-year-old eat cake? Most babies can have a small taste of soft cake at their first birthday. Keep sugar low, avoid honey for babies under one, skip hard decorations and nuts, and check with your paediatrician if your baby has allergies. What size should a smash cake be? A smash cake is usually 10 to 12 cm across, roughly 300 to 500 grams, which is plenty for one enthusiastic baby.

---

# What to Write on a Birthday Cake: 70 Messages That Fit
URL: https://thebakebasket.com/blog/what-to-write-on-a-birthday-cake/

Keep it short: four to six words on a bento cake, up to eight or ten on a 1 kg round, and always check the spelling of the name twice. The best cake messages sound like something you'd actually say to that person, which is why "Happy Birthday" plus a name almost always works, and why a little private joke works even better. Below are seventy ideas, sorted by who the cake is for. Steal freely. When you order on WhatsApp, just copy the line in, and we'll pipe it in a steady hand. If it's a small one, our bento cakes are made for short messages. How much space you really have Cake Comfortable length ------ Bento (about 10 cm) 3 to 6 words 500 g round 5 to 8 words 1 kg round 6 to 10 words 2 kg and up A name, a line, and room for a small drawing Long names take up more room than you think. "Happy Birthday Venkataraghavan" is a full cake on its own. For Amma 1. Happy birthday, Amma 2. Best Amma ever 3. For the one who fed us all 4. Amma, you're still the boss 5. Happy 60th, our forever girl 6. Thank you for everything, Ma 7. To the heart of our home 8. Amma: 60 and fabulous 9. From your favourite (don't tell the others) 10. All our love, today and always For Appa 11. Happy birthday, Appa 12. Our first hero 13. Appa, 65 and still right 14. To the man with all the answers 15. Love you, Appa For your partner 21. Still you. Always. 22. Happy birthday, my person 23. Year 35. Still my favourite. 24. You + me + cake 25. Thanks for putting up with me 26. Happy birthday, handsome 27. Happy birthday, gorgeous 28. Grow old with me (slowly) 29. My best decision 30. Ok fine, you're right For kids 31. Happy 5th, superstar 32. Roar! You're 4! 33. The birthday princess is here 34. Captain Arjun, age 7 35. Look who's ONE 36. Happy birthday, little monkey 37. Ten whole years of Meera 38. Happy birthday to our sunshine 39. Big girl now! 40. You're our favourite surprise For teenagers (who will pretend not to care) 41. Happy 13th. Don't roll your eyes. 42. Officially a teenager 43. Sweet sixteen, finally 44. Yes, we got the cake you wanted 45. 18 and free (almost) For friends 46. Happy birthday, partner in crime 47. Older but not wiser 48. Thirty, flirty and thriving 49. Still the best gossip in town 50. Here's to many more chai breaks 51. My forever plus one 52. Happy birthday, legend 53. Another year of tolerating me For colleagues 54. Happy birthday from Team Ops 55. Happy work birthday! 56. Thanks for all the late nights 57. You make Mondays better 58. Enjoy your day off (we'll manage) 59. Best manager, no pressure 60. Happy retirement, finally! Funny ones 61. Calories don't count today 62. Age is just a number. Yours is big. 63. Keep calm, it's only one more year 64. Don't count the candles 65. Officially vintage 66. You're not old, you're classic For grandparents 67. Happy 80th, Thatha 68. Paati: still the best cook (after this cake) 69. 75 years of being wonderful 70. To our Ammachi, with all our love A few practical tips Write it exactly as you want it. Capitals, punctuation and emojis included. If you want "Happy Birthday AMMA!!" or "happy birthday amma", say so. Send the name in writing. Names said over a voice note get misspelt more often than you'd think, especially names with several common spellings, like Sindhu, Sindu and Sindhoo. Consider a topper for long messages. A printed or acrylic topper can carry more words without crowding the cake. The note is a second chance. If the message you want is longer, write it on the handwritten Basket Note that comes with every order and keep the cake short. What is the best thing to write on a birthday cake? "Happy Birthday" with the person's name is the classic and almost always right. For something more personal, add a short line that sounds like you, such as a nickname, an age or an inside joke. How many words fit on a cake? A bento cake fits about three to six words, a 1 kg round cake six to ten. Longer messages fit better on a topper or a card. What should I write on my mother's birthday cake? Short, warm lines work best, such as "Best Amma ever", "Happy 60th, Amma" or "To the heart of our home".

# Planning a Kids' Theme Cake That Tastes as Good as It Looks
URL: https://thebakebasket.com/blog/kids-theme-birthday-cake-planning/

Start with the child, not the picture. Ask what they love this year, choose two or three colours and one hero element, and let the baker build the rest around a flavour your guests will actually eat. Most disappointing theme cakes go wrong because they try to fit a whole film onto the top of a 1 kg cake. Dinosaurs, rockets, unicorns, cricket pitches, mermaids, construction sites: every child has a world they want on their cake. Here's how I plan them so the six-year-old gasps and the adults ask for a second slice. If you'd like to see options first, our custom cakes page has more. Start with one hero Every good theme cake has one thing your eye goes to first. A dinosaur. A rocket. A crown. A cricket bat crossed with a stump. Everything else supports it: the colours, a few small details, the child's name and age. When there's no hero, the cake turns into a crowded collage. When there are three heroes, they fight for space and none of them look right. So if your daughter loves unicorns, rainbows, mermaids and kittens, ask her which one is the birthday. The others can go on the plates. Pick the colours early Two or three colours, maybe four. That's it. Give them as real examples: "the blue of her school uniform", "the green in the party banner". Bright colours like deep red, navy and black need a lot of colouring, which can affect taste, so I tend to use them only for accents. Pastels and soft brights photograph beautifully and taste the same as a plain cake. Let the finish follow the design This is where theme cakes often go wrong. Parents ask for a fully fondant-covered cake because that's what the pictures online show, and then half the children peel off the fondant and the cake looks like a crime scene by the second slice. My rule of thumb: - Buttercream or cream finish for the cake itself. It tastes good and children eat it. - Fondant only for figures and toppers: the dinosaur, the crown, the number. These can be made ahead and kept as a souvenir. - Printed edible images only where a flat picture is the point. They're quick but look flat next to piped work. There's a longer explanation in fondant vs buttercream vs fresh cream. About characters Many children ask for a favourite cartoon or film character. I'm happy to make a cake inspired by the theme, using the colours, the setting, the props and the feeling, without copying a trademarked character exactly. A "space adventure" cake with a rocket, planets and your child's name is still their dream cake, and often looks more special than a copy of a toy box. Choose a flavour for the guests The child will eat a few bites of frosting and wander off to play. The adults and older children will eat the cake. So pick the flavour for them. Chocolate truffle, butterscotch and vanilla with fresh fruit are the safest choices for a mixed crowd. If several guests are eggless, consider making the whole cake eggless so nobody gets a different slice. Size: count everybody Count every child and every adult. Children's parties eat more cake than you expect. For 20 children and 15 adults, I'd plan 3 to 3.5 kg, or a 2 kg theme cake plus cupcakes in matching colours. See how much cake do you need. What to send your baker Make it easy and you'll get a better cake: 1. Child's name, age and the date 2. The theme, in one sentence 3. The hero element 4. Colours 5. Two or three reference pictures, plus a photo of the invitation or decorations 6. Guest count 7. Flavour, eggless or not, any allergies 8. Where the cake will be and when it'll be cut On the day Keep the cake in the fridge until about 20 minutes before cutting, or in an air-conditioned room if it has a lot of fondant. Place it away from windows and the hall's spotlights. Take the photos first, then cut. And save the fondant figure. A surprising number of them end up on a shelf for years. How far in advance should I order a kids' theme cake? At The Bake Basket, order at least 2 days ahead for a buttercream theme cake, and about a week ahead if the design has fondant figures that need time to set. Can you make a cake with a cartoon character? We make cakes inspired by your child's favourite theme, with matching colours, settings and props. We don't copy trademarked characters exactly, but the cake will still feel like their favourite story. What's the best cake for a kids' party? Chocolate truffle, vanilla with fresh fruit and butterscotch are the most popular. Choose a buttercream or cream finish so the children actually eat the cake, and use fondant only for toppers.

# Anniversary Cakes for Your Parents: Ideas for 25th, 40th and 50th
URL: https://thebakebasket.com/blog/anniversary-cake-ideas-for-parents/

For a parents' anniversary, choose a cake that looks elegant rather than flashy, in a flavour their generation loves, at a size that also covers the relatives who will "just drop in". Silver (25th), ruby (40th) and golden (50th) anniversaries each have their own colour, which makes the design easy. The message matters more than the decoration. The colours, by year Anniversary Traditional name Colour ideas --------- 25th Silver White and silver, pearl, soft grey 30th Pearl Ivory, cream, pearl details 40th Ruby Deep red, maroon, white with ruby roses 50th Golden Ivory and gold, champagne, gold leaf touches 60th Diamond White, silver, crystal-like sugar work These aren't rules. If your mother's favourite colour is the peacock blue of her wedding saree, that's a better idea than any list. Designs that work The photo cake, done well. An edible print of the wedding photo, framed in piped buttercream. It sounds simple. When the couple sees it, it usually isn't. The saree border. A buttercream or fondant border that echoes the design of the wedding saree or the veshti's zari. A beautiful, quietly personal detail. Two tiers, two stories. One tier for the wedding year, one for now. A mini figure of their first scooter, the house they first lived in, the year printed on the side. Fresh flowers or piped florals. Jasmine-white, rose and gold. Always elegant. (We use food-safe flowers only, kept away from the cake surface where needed.) Simple and confident. A single-tier cake, smooth ivory buttercream, a gold "50" and their names. Sometimes less really is more. Flavours for an older crowd Many parents' generation grew up with fresh cream cakes and fruit flavours, and often find heavy buttercream and rich chocolate too much. Good choices: - Pineapple, the 1980s and 90s favourite - Butterscotch with crunch - Vanilla with fresh fruit - Black Forest, the classic party cake of their era - Rasmalai, for a dessert that feels Indian and festive If one or both parents watch their sugar, ask for a reduced-sugar cake, or keep the main cake small and add a box of jaggery or millet bakes for them. There's more on this in our post on choosing a cake when someone has diabetes. Messages Anniversary cakes often carry the shortest and most moving messages. A few ideas: - "50 years of us" - "Still holding hands" - "Happy 25th, Amma and Appa" - "Thank you for showing us how" - "Since 1976" - "Our love story starts with yours" Make it a basket For parents who don't care much about cake, a basket can mean more. A small anniversary cake, a box of the cookies they love, a loaf of brioche for the morning after, and a handwritten note from each grandchild. It arrives in a real basket, and they'll keep it. See our gift hampers. If you're far away Plenty of anniversary cakes are ordered by children living in another city or country. You can order on WhatsApp and pay online, and we'll let you know when it's delivered. Our guide on sending a cake to Chennai from abroad explains how. What is the colour for a 25th wedding anniversary cake? The 25th anniversary is the silver jubilee, so white and silver are the traditional colours. Pearl, soft grey and ivory also work well. What cake flavour do older parents prefer? Many prefer lighter fresh cream cakes in flavours like pineapple, butterscotch, Black Forest and vanilla with fruit, rather than heavy buttercream or very rich chocolate. How big should a 50th anniversary cake be? Count every guest and add a little for visitors. A family gathering of 20 to 25 needs about 2 kg; a hall celebration of 80 to 100 guests needs 7 to 10 kg, often as tiers.
