# What to Take When Visiting a New Baby
URL: https://thebakebasket.com/blog/what-to-take-when-visiting-new-baby/

Take food for the parents, not a toy for the baby. New parents in the first few weeks are tired, often unable to cook, and receiving a stream of visitors. A basket of easy, one-handed food (banana bread, savoury muffins, soft bread, cookies) helps more than another soft toy. Message before you go, keep the visit short, and don't expect to hold the baby. Our new baby baskets are built around exactly this. Why food beats toys Babies get dozens of toys and outfits in the first month. Many go unused, and most are outgrown in weeks. Food, on the other hand, solves an immediate problem: the parents need to eat, and they have neither the time nor the energy. A new mother breastfeeding at 3 am will be grateful for a muffin she can eat with one hand. A father who has been in and out of the pharmacy all day will be grateful for a loaf of bread and something to put on it. What to put in One-handed snacks. Muffins (sweet and savoury), banana bread, cookies, date and nut bars. Things you can eat while holding a baby. Breakfast. Soft bread, a whole-wheat loaf, brioche. Breakfast is often the meal that disappears entirely in the newborn weeks. Something for visitors. A cake or cookie tin to offer the endless stream of relatives, so the parents don't have to go out and buy something. Something nourishing. Many Indian families have traditional postpartum foods: ragi, sesame, ghee, dry ginger, garlic. If you know the family's traditions, ask before bringing these, as the grandmothers usually have strong views. Ask about diet New mothers in many Indian families follow a postpartum diet for several weeks, avoiding certain foods. Some avoid cold food, some avoid certain vegetables, many eat specific confinement foods. Ask a family member what's welcome before you send something. Other useful gifts - Ready meals or a food delivery voucher - An offer to run an errand - A pack of the nappies they use (ask the size) - Something for older siblings, who often feel left out - A small gift for the mother herself: a book, a nice shawl, a skincare treat Visiting etiquette - Message first. Always. And accept "not this week" gracefully. - Keep it short. Twenty to thirty minutes is plenty. - Wash your hands as soon as you arrive. - Don't visit if you're unwell, even a mild cold. - Don't expect to hold the baby. If you're offered, lovely. - Offer to help. Wash a few dishes, fold some laundry, make tea. - Don't give unsolicited advice. They're getting plenty. If you can't visit Send the basket anyway. A delivery with a handwritten note that says "Congratulations, no need to reply" is one of the kindest things you can do. What should I bring when visiting a newborn? Bring food for the parents, such as banana bread, savoury muffins, soft bread or cookies, which can be eaten easily with one hand. Check with the family before bringing anything, and keep the visit short. What is a good gift for new parents in India? Easy food baskets, ready meals, practical items like nappies, and a small gift for the mother are all appreciated. Ask about postpartum diet traditions before sending food. Is it okay to visit a newborn in the first week? Only if the parents invite you. Many families prefer fewer visitors in the first weeks. Always message first and never visit if you're unwell.

# How to Send a Birthday Cake to Your Parents in Chennai From Abroad
URL: https://thebakebasket.com/blog/send-cake-to-parents-in-chennai-from-abroad/

To send a birthday cake to your parents in Chennai from abroad, choose a Chennai baker who takes WhatsApp orders, share the date, address and a contact number for your parents (or a neighbour), pay online, and ask for a photo or video when it's delivered. Order at least two days ahead, time the delivery for when someone is definitely home, and write the message yourself. Plenty of Chennai birthday cakes are ordered by sons and daughters in Bengaluru, Dubai, Singapore, London, Toronto and the US. Here's how to make it go smoothly. You can start right away on our how to order page. Step 1: Pick the right day and time Time zones catch people out. If you're in the US, your evening is your parents' next morning. Confirm the date in India time. Then pick a delivery window when someone is home and awake. Many older parents nap in the afternoon. A late-morning or early-evening delivery is usually safest. If it's a surprise, coordinate with a sibling, neighbour or helper who can receive it. Step 2: Give complete details The most common reason a delivery goes wrong is an incomplete address. Share: - Full address, with flat number, block, landmark and PIN code - A phone number for someone at the address - A backup number (a neighbour, the building security, a sibling in the city) - Anything the delivery person should know: "ring the bell twice", "Amma doesn't hear the phone", "security needs a name" Step 3: Choose something they'll love, not something that looks good on Instagram Think about what your parents actually enjoy. Many older parents prefer lighter cakes, fresh cream rather than buttercream, fruit flavours, less sugar. A big fondant creation might impress you; a soft pineapple cake might impress them. Good choices for parents: - A 500 g cake in their favourite flavour - A bento cake with a short message, if it's just the two of them - A reduced-sugar or millet cake if either watches their sugar - A basket with a small cake, cookies, bread and something traditional If they love traditional food, a box of kozhukattai, vattayappam or puttu from our traditional steamed foods can mean more than any cake. Step 4: Write the message yourself Don't let the baker guess. Send the exact words for the cake (short) and the note (longer). The Basket Note that comes with every order is handwritten, which matters to parents more than you might think. A few ideas: - On the cake: "Happy 70th, Appa" / "Love you, Amma" - In the note: "Wish I could be there to cut this with you. Save me a slice. Calling you tonight." Step 5: Pay online Most Chennai home bakers accept UPI, which needs an Indian bank account. If you don't have one, ask about a payment link that accepts international cards, or ask a family member in India to pay. Step 6: Ask for proof of delivery Ask for a photo or short video when it's delivered. Better still, arrange a video call for the moment it arrives. Watching your mother open a box from three thousand kilometres away is not the same as being there, but it's closer than you'd think. Step 7: Book the next one Birthdays, anniversaries, Mother's Day, Pongal, Onam, Deepavali, Christmas. If you're far away, put the dates in your calendar with a reminder a week before. How can I send a cake to Chennai from the USA? Contact a Chennai baker who takes WhatsApp orders, share your parents' full address, contact numbers, delivery date and message, pay online by card or payment link, and ask for a delivery photo. Can I pay for a Chennai cake order with an international card? Many bakers accept international cards through a payment link. UPI usually requires an Indian bank account. Ask the baker which options they offer. How do I make sure my parents are home for the delivery? Choose a late-morning or early-evening slot, give a backup contact number, and coordinate with a sibling, neighbour or helper if it's a surprise.

# Corporate Deepavali Gifting in Chennai: Ideas That Get Remembered
URL: https://thebakebasket.com/blog/corporate-deepavali-gifting-chennai/

The corporate Deepavali gifts people remember are personal, useful, and different from the dry-fruit box every company sends. A food basket with fresh bakes, a mix of sweet and savoury, clear labels, a handwritten card, and delivery to the recipient's home stands out. Plan four weeks ahead for quantities over 50, and confirm diet needs before finalising. We handle these through our corporate and bulk orders desk. Why most corporate gifts are forgotten Every Deepavali, the same box arrives: almonds, cashews, raisins, a candle, a cellophane window. It's not unwelcome, but it isn't memorable either. By the third one, it all blends together. Gifts that get remembered tend to have one of three things: they're made by someone, they're useful at home, or they come with a personal touch. What works Fresh food baskets. Cookies, brownies, a fruit cake, savoury bites, a small traditional sweet. They're shared at home, which is where Deepavali happens. A real basket. Reusable, kept, and associated with your company every time it's used. A handwritten card. Even a short line from the team lead makes a difference. Delivery to home. Many employees and clients are on leave or working from home during Deepavali week. A basket that sits on an office desk over a long weekend isn't much of a gift. Budgets Tier Typical recipient What it might include --------- Entry Wider team, vendors Cookie tin or brownie box with a card Standard Employees Small basket: cookies, brownies, savoury, a sweet Premium Key clients, leadership Larger basket: cake, cookies, brownies, savoury, bread, something traditional Diet and labelling In any Chennai office, you'll have vegetarians, eggless families, people avoiding sugar, and the occasional nut allergy. Collect this before ordering, or make the whole order eggless and nut-free with clear labels. Every item should be labelled: veg, eggless, contains nuts, contains gluten. Logistics Timeline. Confirm the order and list three to four weeks before Deepavali. Deliveries usually go out in the five days before the festival. Address list. Collect home addresses with phone numbers in a spreadsheet. Missing PIN codes and landmarks cause most delivery problems. Delivery days. Spread deliveries over a few days rather than all on the eve of the festival. Card. Agree on card text early. Personalised cards (with each person's name) take longer than a single message. Invoicing. Confirm GST invoicing needs and PO numbers in advance. A word on sustainability Many companies now avoid plastic-heavy gifts. A cane basket, paper wrapping, glass jars and no plastic windows are easy wins that people notice. What are good corporate Deepavali gifts in Chennai? Fresh food baskets with cookies, brownies, savoury snacks and a traditional sweet, packed in a reusable basket with a personal card, are memorable and widely appreciated. When should companies order Deepavali hampers? For more than 50 hampers, place the order three to four weeks before Deepavali. Smaller orders need about two weeks. Should corporate gifts be delivered to the office or home? Home delivery is usually better during Deepavali week, as many people are on leave or working from home and the gift is shared with family.

# Thank-You Gifts for Teachers That Aren't Another Mug
URL: https://thebakebasket.com/blog/thank-you-gifts-for-teachers/

The thank-you gifts teachers value most are a heartfelt note from the child and something small they can enjoy or share: a tin of cookies, a box of brownies, a loaf of banana bread. Teachers get a lot of mugs, pens and keyrings. They rarely get something homemade with a child's own words on it. In India, Teachers' Day is 5 September, the birthday of Dr S. Radhakrishnan. The end of the school year and the last day before a teacher leaves are the other big moments. Our brownies and cookies are a popular choice for all three. What teachers say they value Ask a few teachers and you'll hear the same thing. The note matters most. A card in a child's handwriting, or a drawing, gets kept for years. Many teachers have a folder of them. After the note, what's appreciated is something consumable. Teachers have a finite number of shelves. They don't have a finite appetite for good cookies. Ideas that work Name cookies. A tin of cookies with "Thank you, Ms Lakshmi" iced on top. Personal, edible, photographable. A brownie box. Teachers often share with colleagues in the staff room, which makes a box of brownies doubly appreciated. Banana bread or a tea cake. Something for the teacher's own family at home. A small basket from the whole class. Parents pool together for one generous basket with cookies, a cake, savoury snacks and a card signed by every child. One thoughtful gift beats thirty small ones. A plant with a note. Not edible, but lasting. Something for the staff room. A tray of cupcakes or puffs for all the teachers. A lovely gesture from a class's parents, and the support staff appreciate it too. A few etiquette notes - Check the school's policy. Some schools discourage individual gifts or set a limit. Many prefer a class gift. - Keep it modest. Expensive gifts can make teachers uncomfortable. - Avoid nuts if the school is nut-free; the staff room counts too. - Don't forget the others. Ayahs, bus attendants, security and the office staff look after your child too. Write the note together Sit with your child and ask: "What do you want to say to your teacher?" Write down their words, not yours. "Thank you for helping me with fractions" is better than anything a parent could write. If your child is young, a drawing with a short line ("You are kind") is perfect. What is a good thank-you gift for a teacher? A handwritten note from the child with a small consumable gift, such as cookies, brownies or banana bread, is thoughtful and appreciated. A class gift pooled by parents also works well. When is Teachers' Day in India? Teachers' Day in India is celebrated on 5 September, the birthday of Dr Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan. How much should I spend on a teacher's gift? Keep it modest. Many schools discourage expensive gifts, and teachers value the personal note far more than the price. A class gift lets parents contribute a small amount each.

# Edible Return Gifts for Kids' Birthday Parties
URL: https://thebakebasket.com/blog/edible-return-gifts-kids-birthday/

Edible return gifts are often a better choice than toys: they're eaten instead of forgotten in a drawer, they match the party theme, and they're easy to personalise. Popular options are iced name cookies, mini brownie boxes, a single cupcake in a box, cookie jars, and small treat bags. Order a week ahead for decorated items, and always label anything with nuts or egg. See our brownies and cookies and cupcakes for the range. Why edible? Think about the last ten plastic return gifts your child brought home. How many are still in use? Edible gifts get enjoyed, photographed, and talked about. They also make a lovely last impression of the party. Ideas, by budget Small budget - Two or three cookies in a printed bag - A single brownie, individually wrapped, with a sticker Medium budget - Iced name cookies (each child's name), packed in a bag or box - A mini box of four brownies or cookies - One cupcake in a clear box, in the party's colours Generous - A cookie jar with a mix of cookies and a name tag - A small box with a cupcake, two cookies and a brownie - A theme set: cookies shaped like the party theme Matching the theme Edible gifts can echo the party: dinosaur cookies for a dinosaur party, rainbow sprinkles for a rainbow theme, stars and moons for "little star". Iced cookies are the easiest way to do this. Send your baker the invitation or a photo of the decorations. Plan for allergies Ask parents about allergies when they RSVP, or simply make the return gifts nut-free and label egg. A small sticker on each bag ("contains egg, wheat, milk") is responsible and appreciated. Practical tips - Count siblings. Children often bring a brother or sister; order five or ten extra. - Keep them cool. Chocolate-coated items melt in a car; choose cookies and plain brownies. - Hand them out at the end, not the start, or they'll be eaten before the cake. - Add a thank-you tag with the birthday child's name: "Thank you for coming to Aarav's 6th!" Combine with a non-edible Some parents like to add a small useful item: a pencil, a mini notebook, a crayon set, a seed packet. Paired with cookies, it feels complete. What are good return gifts for a kids' birthday party? Edible return gifts like iced name cookies, mini brownie boxes and cupcakes in a box are popular because they're enjoyed rather than forgotten. Small useful items like crayons or notebooks also pair well. How far in advance should I order return gift cookies? Order decorated or name cookies at least a week before the party. Plain cookie bags and brownies need two to three days. Are edible return gifts safe for children with allergies? Check with parents about allergies, choose nut-free options where possible, and label every bag with allergens such as egg, wheat and milk.

# Fudgy or Cakey? What Makes a Brownie a Brownie
URL: https://thebakebasket.com/blog/fudgy-vs-cakey-brownies/

Fudgy brownies have more fat and chocolate relative to flour, little or no raising agent, and are baked just until set. Cakey brownies have more flour, often baking powder, more beaten-in air, and a longer bake. The shiny, crackly top comes from dissolving sugar well into warm butter and eggs and beating it briefly before the flour goes in. I have strong views on this. I make fudgy brownies, the kind that stick a little to your fingers and taste even better on day two. You can find them on our brownies and cookies page. But both types are real brownies, and a lot of people love the cakey kind. Here's what decides which one you get. The ratio Everything starts with the balance of fat (butter and chocolate) to flour. Fudgy: lots of butter and chocolate, very little flour. The flour is there to hold it together, barely. Cakey: more flour, less fat. The texture moves towards a chocolate cake. Chewy: somewhere in between, often with more egg, brown sugar or a little oil. Chocolate or cocoa Melted chocolate adds fat and cocoa solids, which make a denser, richer, fudgier brownie. Cocoa powder adds intense chocolate flavour without the fat, so cocoa-only brownies tend to be cakier unless you add more butter. I use both: dark chocolate for texture, a spoonful of cocoa for depth. Raising agents Fudgy brownies usually have none. Cakey brownies often have baking powder, which lifts them into a lighter, airier crumb. Eggs and beating Eggs bind and add structure. Beating eggs with sugar for a long time adds air, which makes brownies cakier. For fudgy brownies, you beat just enough to dissolve the sugar and create the top, then fold the flour in gently. That crackly top This is the part people ask about most. The thin, papery, shiny crust that shatters when you cut it. It comes from sugar dissolving well into the warm wet ingredients, then rising to the surface as the brownie bakes and setting into a thin meringue-like layer. The tricks: - Use warm melted butter and chocolate, so the sugar dissolves. - Beat the eggs and sugar for a minute or two until the mixture turns slightly glossy and pale. - Don't skimp on sugar; it's what forms the crust. Baking time The biggest mistake is overbaking. Brownies keep cooking from their own heat after they leave the oven. Take fudgy brownies out when the edges are set and the middle still looks slightly soft, and a skewer comes out with a few moist crumbs. Then let them cool fully before cutting. Cutting warm brownies tastes wonderful and looks like a landslide. Day two is better Fudgy brownies firm up and the flavours deepen overnight. If you can wait, wait. If you can't, nobody blames you. Eggless and ragi brownies Eggless brownies can be just as fudgy; curd or condensed milk takes the place of egg, and the high chocolate content does most of the work. Ragi brownies are naturally dense and earthy, which suits fudgy brownies perfectly. More on that in is ragi cake gluten-free. What makes brownies fudgy instead of cakey? Fudgy brownies have a higher ratio of butter and chocolate to flour, little or no baking powder, and a shorter baking time. Cakey brownies have more flour, often baking powder, and more air beaten in. How do you get a crackly top on brownies? Dissolve the sugar into warm melted butter and chocolate, beat with the eggs briefly until glossy, and use enough sugar. The sugar rises and forms a thin, shiny crust as it bakes. Should brownies be gooey in the middle? Fudgy brownies should be moist and dense in the middle but set, not raw. Take them out when a skewer comes out with a few moist crumbs, and let them cool before cutting.

# The Kids' Birthday Party Food Checklist
URL: https://thebakebasket.com/blog/kids-birthday-party-food-checklist/

For a kids' birthday party, plan three kinds of food: easy finger food for the children, something more filling for the adults, and the cake. Keep the children's food small, mild and familiar (mini sandwiches, puffs, fruit, popcorn, cupcakes), plan two to three savoury pieces per child and three to four per adult, and serve the cake about halfway through, before everyone gets restless. Here's the checklist we'd give a friend. For savoury bakes and platters, see savoury bakes and sandwiches. Before you plan the menu - [ ] Final headcount: children and adults separately - [ ] Party length and time of day (lunch? evening?) - [ ] Will adults stay? (In Chennai, usually yes, and they'll eat.) - [ ] Allergies and dietary needs: eggless, nut-free, vegetarian, Jain - [ ] Venue: home, building clubhouse, play area, hall - [ ] Is there a fridge? Ovens? Serving staff? For the children Children at parties eat little and often, mostly whatever they can grab while running. - [ ] Mini sandwiches (cheese chutney, corn cheese, jam) - [ ] Veg puffs or mini pizzas - [ ] Popcorn or chips in small cups - [ ] Fruit (watermelon, grapes, banana), cut small - [ ] Cupcakes or cookies (separate from the cake) - [ ] Juice or flavoured milk in small cups or tetra packs - [ ] Water, lots of it Keep it: small, not spicy, not sticky, not messy. Avoid whole nuts and hard sweets for under-fives. For the adults In most Chennai parties, adults stay and expect proper food, especially in the evening. - [ ] Savoury bakes: puffs, buns, rolls, cutlets - [ ] Sandwiches or a platter - [ ] Something hot if it's close to a meal time: pav bhaji, pasta, biryani, or a full caterer - [ ] Tea and coffee - [ ] Something sweet besides cake The cake - [ ] Size for everyone (see how much cake) - [ ] Eggless if many guests are - [ ] Candles, knife, matches or lighter, cake server, plates - [ ] A spot away from windows and the sun - [ ] Fridge space until 20 minutes before cutting Timing Time What happens ------ Start Welcome drinks, light snacks for early arrivals 30 to 45 min Games; finger food on the table Halfway Cake cutting, photos After cake Main savoury food or meal for adults End Return gifts at the door Cutting the cake halfway keeps young children happy (they've been waiting) and gives older guests the chance to leave after cake if they need to. Quantities, roughly Item Per child Per adult --------- Savoury pieces (puffs, buns) 1 to 2 2 to 3 Sandwich quarters 2 3 to 4 Cupcakes or cookies 1 to 2 1 Drinks 2 cups 2 cups plus tea For an evening party that runs past 7.30 pm, treat it as dinner for adults. More detail in party snack quantities. Make it easier on yourself - Order the savoury bakes and cake from one place, so there's one delivery and one person to call. - Ask for everything to be labelled: veg, egg, contains nuts. - Keep a box of plain biscuits for the child who won't eat anything else. - Have a helper on food duty while you're on host duty. What food should I serve at a kids' birthday party? Serve small, mild finger food for children, like mini sandwiches, puffs, fruit and cupcakes, along with more filling savoury food for adults, and the birthday cake. How much food do I need for a kids' party? Plan about one to two savoury pieces and two sandwich quarters per child, and two to three savoury pieces plus three to four sandwich quarters per adult. For evening parties, serve a proper meal for adults. When should the cake be cut at a kids' party? Cut the cake about halfway through the party, after games and before the main food, when children are still excited and before younger guests get tired.

# Office Birthdays Without the Stress: A Planner for HR and Admin Teams
URL: https://thebakebasket.com/blog/office-birthday-celebration-planner/

The simplest way to run office birthdays is a monthly celebration: one cake or a tray of cupcakes for everyone born that month, on a fixed day, with an eggless option. It's fair, predictable, and easy to budget. For small teams, individual birthdays with a bento cake or cupcakes work well. Either way, confirm diet needs once, set a recurring order, and nominate one person to own it. We set up exactly this kind of standing order through our corporate and bulk orders page. Monthly or individual? Monthly celebrations work best for teams over 20. Everyone born in the month is celebrated together, on, say, the last Friday. One order, one gathering, one set of photos. Individual birthdays work best for small teams under 15, where each person's day can be marked. A bento cake on their desk in the morning, or a box of cupcakes for the team. A hybrid: monthly cake for everyone, plus a small personal touch (a card signed by the team, a bento cake) on the actual day. Set up once, run all year 1. Build a birthday list with names and dates (with permission; some people prefer not to be celebrated, and that's fine). 2. Collect diet needs once: vegetarian, eggless, Jain, diabetic, allergies. 3. Choose a format and day. For example: last Friday of the month, 4 pm, cupcakes plus one cake. 4. Set a budget per month. 5. Set a standing order with a baker, with a reminder a week before. 6. Nominate an owner and a backup. Eggless or not? In most Chennai offices, the answer is simply eggless. It means everyone can eat the same cake, and nobody has to ask. Very few people notice the difference. More in eggless birthday cakes. Cake or cupcakes? Format Pros Cons --------- One cake Classic, good for the cutting moment and photos Needs knife, plates and someone to serve Cupcakes No cutting, no plates, easy for people to grab and go back to desks Less of a "moment" Both Small cake for cutting plus cupcakes for serving Slightly higher cost For teams over 30, "both" is usually best. Quantities Plan about 80 g of cake per person, or one cupcake each plus 10% extra. See how much cake do you need. Timing on the day - Schedule it in calendars as a short meeting so people actually show up. - 4 pm works well: after lunch, before the evening rush. - Ask the baker to deliver 30 to 60 minutes before, and keep cream cakes in the pantry fridge. - Keep it to 15 minutes. A song, a cut, a photo, back to work. Beyond cake Some teams rotate: cake one month, a savoury tea-time box the next, a breakfast spread another. It keeps things fresh and suits people who don't eat sweets. How should offices celebrate employee birthdays? Many offices hold a monthly celebration for everyone born that month, with one cake or cupcakes. Smaller teams often mark each birthday individually with a bento cake or cupcakes. Should office birthday cakes be eggless? In most Chennai offices, choosing an eggless cake is the simplest option, as it lets every colleague share the same cake. How much cake do we need for an office of 40 people? Plan about 3 to 3.5 kg of cake, or one cupcake per person plus a few extra. A small cake for cutting plus cupcakes is a popular combination.

# High Tea at Home: A Menu and How Much to Make
URL: https://thebakebasket.com/blog/high-tea-menu-at-home/

A good high tea has three layers: savoury finger food (sandwiches, puffs, quiche), something baked and plain (scones, tea cake, banana bread), and small sweets (brownies, cupcakes, cookies). Plan four to five savoury pieces, one or two plain bakes and two or three sweets per guest for a two-hour afternoon, plus plenty of tea and something cold for Chennai weather. You can order most of this in one go through our savoury bakes and sandwiches page. What "high tea" means here In Britain, "high tea" originally meant a hearty early-evening meal for working families, and "afternoon tea" was the dainty one. In India, and in Chennai especially, "high tea" has come to mean the dainty version: an afternoon or early-evening spread of small bites with tea. Baby showers, kitty parties, ladies' get-togethers, small engagements, and Sunday afternoons with visiting relatives all qualify. The menu Savoury - Finger sandwiches: cucumber and butter, cheese chutney, egg mayo, chicken, paneer tikka - Mini puffs: veg, egg, chicken - Quiche or savoury tarts: spinach and corn, mushroom - Cheese straws - Mini buns or sliders Plain bakes - Scones with jam and cream, or butter - Tea cake slices: banana walnut, lemon drizzle, marble - Banana bread Sweet - Mini cupcakes - Brownie squares - Butter cookies, nankhatai - Lemon bars - Small tarts Drinks - Tea: a strong Indian tea and something lighter, like Darjeeling or a herbal blend - Filter coffee for the guests who will ask for it - Something cold: iced tea, lemonade, rose milk Quantities per guest (two-hour afternoon) Item Per guest ------ Sandwich pieces (quarters or fingers) 3 to 4 Other savoury pieces 1 to 2 Scone or tea cake slice 1 to 2 Sweet pieces 2 to 3 Tea or coffee 2 cups For 15 guests, that's about 50 sandwich pieces, 20 savouries, 20 plain bakes and 40 sweet pieces. Presentation A tiered stand helps, but a long table with platters at different heights works just as well. Keep savoury and sweet separate. Label anything with egg, nuts or meat. Use real cups if you have them; it makes it an occasion. Timeline When What ------ 2 days before Order bakes and sandwiches; confirm delivery time Day before Plan table, set out crockery, chill drinks 2 hours before Deliveries arrive; cream items in the fridge 30 minutes before Lay out savouries and plain bakes As guests arrive Make tea; bring out sweets after the first round In Chennai heat Keep sandwiches covered and in the fridge until the last moment; they dry out fast. Avoid cream-heavy sweets if the room isn't air-conditioned. Puffs can be warmed in an oven for five minutes just before serving. What food is served at a high tea? A high tea usually includes finger sandwiches and savoury bites, plain bakes like scones and tea cake, and small sweets such as cupcakes, brownies and cookies, served with tea and coffee. How much food do I need for a high tea for 20 people? For 20 guests over two hours, plan around 70 to 80 sandwich pieces, 30 savoury bites, 30 plain bake portions and 50 small sweets. What is the difference between high tea and afternoon tea? Traditionally in Britain, high tea was a hearty evening meal and afternoon tea was the dainty spread. In India, high tea usually refers to the dainty afternoon or evening spread.

# How to Keep a Cake Fresh in Chennai Heat
URL: https://thebakebasket.com/blog/keep-cake-fresh-in-chennai-heat/

In Chennai, assume every cream, buttercream or cheesecake needs the fridge. Keep it boxed in the fridge until 15 to 20 minutes before cutting, carry it flat on the car floor with the AC on, never on a seat or a lap, and keep it out of sunlight and away from hall spotlights. Leftovers go back in the fridge, covered, within two hours. I've had calls from people whose cakes slid in the back of a car on the Kathipara flyover. I've seen a beautiful buttercream cake slowly lean in a glass-walled function hall at 4 pm. Chennai is hard on cakes. Here's how to protect yours. Ordering one? Our how to order page covers delivery. The basic rule Heat and humidity are the enemies. Fresh cream melts. Buttercream softens. Fondant sweats. Chocolate blooms. Every degree matters. Storage by type Type Where How long --------- Fresh whipped cream cake Fridge, boxed 1 to 2 days Buttercream cake Fridge in Chennai; cool AC room for a few hours 2 to 3 days in fridge Cream cheese frosting Fridge always 2 to 3 days Ganache cake Fridge, or cool AC room for a few hours 3 days Fondant cake (with buttercream or ganache under) Cool AC room ideally; if fridge, keep boxed and let condensation evaporate before opening 2 to 3 days Cheesecake Fridge always 3 to 4 days Plain loaf or tea cake Airtight box, room temperature 3 to 4 days Rich plum cake Wrapped, cool place Weeks Brownies and cookies Airtight box, room temperature 4 to 7 days Transporting In a car: - Put the box flat on the floor of the car, not on a seat. Seats slope, and the floor is the coolest, most stable spot. - Turn on the AC before you put the cake in. - Drive gently over speed breakers and on flyover ramps. - Don't leave it in a parked car, even for "five minutes". - If it's a tall or tiered cake, have someone keep a light hand on the box. On a two-wheeler: small cakes, brownies and cookie boxes only, held flat and level, and not in the midday sun. A tall or cream cake on a scooter is a risk we'd rather you didn't take. On foot or in an auto: hold the box from underneath with both hands, flat, like a tray. At the venue - Find the fridge first. If there isn't one, ask for the coolest room. - Keep the cake away from windows, sunlight, kitchens and stage lights. - Leave it in its box until shortly before cutting. - Under the fans? Good. Under the hall's spotlights? Not good. Cutting and serving Take cream and buttercream cakes out of the fridge 15 to 20 minutes before cutting. Cold cake tastes muted; slightly cool cake tastes right. See how to cut a round cake. Storing overnight Cover cut surfaces with cling film or butter paper pressed against the sponge, so it doesn't dry out. Put the cake back in its box, or under a cake dome, in the fridge. Keep it away from strong-smelling food; cream absorbs smells, and nobody wants a slice that tastes faintly of sambar. If it starts to melt Get it into the fridge immediately, for 20 to 30 minutes. Most cakes firm up again. Smooth any slumped frosting with a spatula or the back of a warm spoon. It won't be perfect, but it'll be close, and it'll still taste good. How do you keep a cake from melting in hot weather? Keep it boxed in the fridge until 15 to 20 minutes before serving, away from sunlight and heat. Buttercream and ganache cakes hold up better in heat than fresh cream cakes. How do you transport a cake in a car? Place the box flat on the car floor rather than on a seat, run the AC before and during the drive, drive gently, and never leave the cake in a parked car. Should cake be refrigerated overnight? In a hot, humid city like Chennai, yes. Cover cut surfaces, keep the cake boxed or under a dome, and store it away from strong-smelling food.

# How Many Puffs and Sandwiches Per Person? Party Quantities, Worked Out
URL: https://thebakebasket.com/blog/party-snack-quantities-per-person/

For an evening party where snacks replace a meal, plan 8 to 10 savoury pieces per adult. For snacks before dinner, 4 to 6 pieces. For a working lunch, 4 to 6 sandwich quarters plus 1 to 2 bakes per person. Children eat about half an adult portion. Add 10% for unexpected guests, which, in Chennai, you will have. These are the numbers we use when planning savoury platters. The one question that changes everything Is this food the meal, or is it before or after a meal? Get this wrong and you'll either run out at 8 pm or be eating sandwiches for three days. Snacks before a meal: guests are saving space. Plan light. Snacks instead of a meal: guests arrived hungry and will leave expecting to be full. Tea-time snacks: somewhere in between. The table Occasion Savoury pieces per adult Sandwich quarters per adult Sweets per adult ------------ Snacks before dinner 4 to 6 2 1 to 2 Tea-time (4 to 6 pm) 4 to 6 2 to 3 2 Evening party, no meal (6 to 9 pm) 8 to 10 4 2 to 3 Working lunch 1 to 2 4 to 6 1 Kids' party (per child) 1 to 2 2 1 to 2 "Savoury pieces" means puffs, buns, mini pizzas, cutlets, rolls, quiche slices. Worked examples 30 adults, 6 to 9 pm, no dinner: - 270 savoury pieces (around 9 each), across 4 or 5 kinds - 120 sandwich quarters - 75 sweet pieces - Plus drinks 20 colleagues, working lunch: - 100 sandwich quarters (5 each), mixed veg and non-veg - 30 savoury pieces - 20 cookies or brownies - Fruit 15 children and 15 adults, 4 to 7 pm birthday: - Children: 25 savoury pieces, 30 sandwich quarters, 25 sweets (plus cake) - Adults: 90 savoury pieces, 45 sandwich quarters, 30 sweets - Plus the cake Variety More variety means people try a little of everything, so each item can be smaller in quantity. For 30 people, four or five savoury items is plenty. For 100 people, six to eight. A good mix: one puff, one bun or roll, one baked item (quiche or mini pizza), one fried or crisp item, and sandwiches. Veg and non-veg In Chennai, ask. Many gatherings are fully vegetarian; others are mixed. For mixed groups, plan around 60% vegetarian unless you know otherwise, pack veg and non-veg separately, and label clearly. The 10% rule Add 10% to every count. Someone will bring a cousin. Someone else will be "just passing". It's Chennai. How many snacks per person for a party? For snacks before a meal, plan 4 to 6 savoury pieces per adult. For an evening party where snacks replace dinner, plan 8 to 10 pieces per adult, plus sandwiches and sweets. How many sandwiches per person for a lunch? For a working lunch, plan 4 to 6 sandwich quarters per person, plus one or two savoury bakes and something sweet. How much food do I need for 50 guests? For an evening party with no dinner, plan around 450 savoury pieces, 200 sandwich quarters and 125 sweets for 50 adults. For snacks before dinner, roughly half that.

# Is It Safe to Order From a Home Baker? How to Check FSSAI and Hygiene
URL: https://thebakebasket.com/blog/is-home-baker-safe-fssai/

Yes, a registered home baker can be every bit as safe as a shop, and often fresher. Check three things: that the baker has an FSSAI registration (a 14-digit number you can verify on the FSSAI FoSCoS portal), that they can tell you plainly how they handle hygiene and storage, and that they're open about ingredients and allergens. If a baker won't answer those questions, order elsewhere. I get asked this, gently, by new customers. I'm always glad. It means they care about what they're feeding their family, which is exactly how I feel about it. Our FAQ has our own answers. Why home bakers need FSSAI registration In India, anyone running a food business, including from home, needs to be registered with the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI). Small home bakers typically hold a Basic Registration; larger operations need a State or Central licence. In Tamil Nadu, the state's Food Safety Department, under the Commissioner of Food Safety, administers registration and enforcement. Delivery apps also require an FSSAI number before a baker can list. The thresholds and rules have been updated over the years, so check the current requirements on the FSSAI website rather than relying on older articles. How to check a baker's FSSAI number 1. Ask the baker for their 14-digit FSSAI registration or licence number. It should be on their website, social profile or packaging. 2. Go to the FSSAI FoSCoS portal (foscos.fssai.gov.in). 3. Use the "FBO search" option and enter the number. 4. Check that the name and address match the baker, and that the registration is active. That takes two minutes and tells you the business is on the record. What registration does and doesn't tell you Registration means the baker has declared their business and agreed to follow food safety rules. It doesn't mean someone inspects every kitchen every week. So it's the starting point, not the whole answer. Questions worth asking Any good home baker will be happy to answer these: - How do you store ingredients? Look for sealed containers, a dedicated fridge or shelf, attention to expiry dates. - How do you keep the baking area clean? Clean, dedicated surfaces; hair covered; hands washed; pets kept out of the kitchen. - Do you bake to order, or ahead? Baking to order means fresher food. - How do you handle eggless and allergies? Separate utensils, honest answers about cross-contact. - How do you pack and transport? Food-grade boxes, cold handling for cream cakes. Red flags - No FSSAI number, or reluctance to share it - Photos that are clearly someone else's (reverse-image search if unsure) - Claims that sound too good: "100% organic", "zero sugar", "chemical-free", with no detail - Prices far below everyone else's for the same thing - No clear answer about ingredients or allergens - Asking you to pay a different number or account from the one you've been ordering on (a common scam) Why home bakers often win on freshness A shop counter has to bake ahead. A home baker who bakes to order doesn't. Your cake might have been made this morning rather than two days ago. That's one of the main reasons families in Chennai have moved towards home bakers, along with the personal touch. More on that in why fresh-to-order matters. Do home bakers need FSSAI registration? Yes. Home bakers in India need FSSAI registration to sell food legally. Most small home bakers hold a Basic Registration, and delivery apps require an FSSAI number before listing. How can I check if a home baker is FSSAI registered? Ask for their 14-digit FSSAI number and search it on the FSSAI FoSCoS portal (foscos.fssai.gov.in) using the FBO search. Check that the name and address match. Is food from a home bakery safe? Food from a registered home bakery that follows good hygiene can be just as safe as shop-bought food, and often fresher. Check the FSSAI registration and ask how the baker handles hygiene and storage.

# Why Fresh-to-Order Matters: What Happens to a Cake in a Display Case
URL: https://thebakebasket.com/blog/why-fresh-to-order-cakes-matter/

A cake baked to order reaches you within hours of being finished. A cake from a display case has usually been baked a day or more earlier, and has to be made to survive that wait: often with more sugar, stabilisers or emulsifiers, or premixes designed for shelf life, and frostings built to hold their shape under lights. Fresh-to-order cakes can use simpler ingredients and taste of what's actually in them. That's the reason I bake only after you order. It's also why our custom cakes need a little notice. Here's what's going on behind the glass. The life of a display cake A bakery with a counter has a problem: it needs a full case of cakes when the shop opens, but it doesn't know which ones will sell. So it bakes ahead, in batches. Sponges are baked, cooled, wrapped and stored. Frostings are made in big tubs. Cakes are assembled in the morning, or the night before, and then sit under lights until someone buys them, which might be in an hour, or tomorrow. To make that work, the cake has to be designed to last. What that can mean in the recipe Not every bakery does all of this, and many do none. But these are common in commercial baking: - Premixes. Ready-made cake mixes are consistent, quick and designed for shelf life. They often include emulsifiers and stabilisers so the sponge stays soft for days. - Non-dairy whipped toppings. Many bakery "cream" cakes use vegetable-fat whipped topping rather than dairy cream, because it holds shape longer and doesn't need to be as cold. It tastes sweeter and leaves a slightly waxy feel. - Sugar syrups. Sponges are soaked in syrup to stop them drying out on display. That's partly why bakery cakes can taste very sweet. - Preservatives in fillings and some sponges. None of this is unsafe. It's simply what it takes to sell a cake that was made yesterday. What changes when you bake to order When a cake is going straight from the kitchen to a family, it doesn't have to survive the wait. So it can be made differently: - A sponge from scratch, with butter or oil, eggs or curd, and flour, and nothing else it doesn't need. - Real dairy cream, which tastes cleaner and lighter, and only needs to hold for the time it takes to reach you and be cut. - Less syrup, because the sponge is still fresh. - Fruit that's fresh, not tinned, where the season allows. - Frosting made for that one cake. You can taste it. The sponge is softer and smells of butter. The cream tastes of cream. The cake is less sweet, so you can taste the chocolate, or the coffee, or the mango. The trade-off Fresh-to-order needs planning. You can't walk in at 7 pm and pick a cake off a shelf. You'll need to order a day or a few days ahead, depending on what you want. See how far ahead to order a custom cake. And because the cake is fresh, it's also more delicate. Real cream doesn't hold up like vegetable topping does in the heat, so it needs a fridge and some care on the drive. There's a guide to that in keeping a cake fresh in Chennai heat. Why I think it's worth it Because the cake is for a moment that matters. The candles, the song, the first bite, the little silence before someone says "this is so good". That moment deserves a cake made for it, on the day, by someone who knows who's going to eat it. That's all fresh-to-order really means. A cake that was waiting for no one but you. What is the difference between a fresh-baked cake and a bakery cake? A fresh-baked-to-order cake is made after you order and delivered within hours. Many bakery display cakes are baked ahead and may use premixes, stabilisers, non-dairy toppings or syrups so they stay fresh-looking for longer. Why does homemade cake taste better? Homemade, baked-to-order cakes often use simpler ingredients like real butter and dairy cream, less syrup and fresh fruit, because they don't need to survive days on display. That gives a cleaner, less sweet taste. Do bakery cakes have preservatives? Some do, and many use premixes, stabilisers or non-dairy whipped toppings to extend shelf life. Not all bakeries use these, so ask if it matters to you.
